UnderstandingPrompt: Personal denars are funds held by individual heroes, not virtual treasuries of clans, parties or settlements. The player and policy publisher may also be direct character targets. When policies reasonably and directly change personal economic gains through army pay, salaries, trade, industry income, subsidies, rewards, punishments or confiscations, personal denars are the actual consequence. The model independently judges affected characters or native professions; policies need not name professions or exact amounts verbatim. Local army pay, salaries, allowances or fiscal subsidies without another specified personal recipient default to the current owner-clan leader of the affected settlement; retain settlement-bound targets. Use character targets only when the body directly names individuals or professions. Continuing income, stipends, salaries, allowances and regular subsidies are usually ongoing changes; rewards, bonuses, back pay, fines and confiscations are usually one-time changes. Interpret income as fief taxation only when the body explicitly involves fiefs, towns, castles or taxation. Publication and upkeep costs, construction investment and general administrative budgets are excluded.
EvaluationPrompt: One-time changes settle on the game day after policy adoption; daily changes settle each day while the policy is valid. Values apply per final character, not to a group total. Positive values are independent income or subsidies; negatives are personal burdens, fines or confiscations. Do not create character-to-character transfers. When the body gives no amount, choose concrete integers from wording intensity, policy coverage and resource commitments, rather than mechanically using range midpoints. Mild or limited daily income changes are usually ±50 to ±150 per person; regular explicit income policies ±150 to ±500; major or generous long-term policies ±500 to ±1500; only extreme, well-supported policies reach ±1500 to ±5000. Small one-time rewards or fines are usually ±500 to ±2000 per person; significant dispositions ±2000 to ±10000; major rewards or confiscations ±10000 to ±50000. Generic increases to lords' income should produce positive daily changes without additional one-time changes. Do not divide a group total among individuals because many targets exist, or count policy costs again as personal balance changes.
